institutionName: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to a place with beautiful nature, possibilites to do a lot of sports and a country which isn't too far away since it's nice to be able to visit it again easily.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The website of the university was very helpful, and it was possible to contact them if needed. Other students which were on exchange from KU could also help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Orientation week where we got to know the campus, different student organisations and how to access all host university platforms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was easy, but I think I might have been lucky. I started to look for a place to live around 3 months before my exchange, and I was lucky to get a room the second place i contacted. Others that I know, contacted many places and struggled more than me. I think it's good to look in advance of your exchange, and be patient when writing to people. But don't worry if you don't find anything in the beginning, it will work out somehow.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
I liked living off campus and in the city center since it was so easy to walk around and get to the center from everywhere. The city center wasn't too far away from my campus, but it depends on which campus you're going so check for that as well before your stay.
Furthermore I liked that the city center wasn't that far away from nature, so it's possible to go hiking without having to travel too far. But if you like nature, it's also possible to live closer to the fjell.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was possible to live at some of the student villages if someone rented out their room for a while, and I heard it's pretty nice to live there as well since there are many exchange students and the accomodations are quite good. But for me, living in the city center was best, as the student cities are a bit further away.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
NTNU will send you mails with your account and information about how to register for courses when it's time. You get an account at
studentweb.no
(if your host university is NTNU), and then you can register for courses in the website under "active courses".
You can change your courses until two weeks after the courses have started, therefore it's possible to see if you like the course or not.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: NTNUs website is really helpful and it's possible to contact their international office for help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I registered for all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: NTNU has a lot of international students and receive a lot of mails every day, so I would suggest looking at their website or asking other students how to do things before writing them an e-mail as the response time can be quite long before the exchange.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level is really good, I would say the standards are the same as the Copenhagen University.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had both bachelor and master level courses. The master level (second degree level course) (Immunology) was very good, and it was not a problem to follow along.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It depends on how much you're used to self studying. I didn't have any laboratory work, so only lectures and group exercises which meant that there was a lot of self studying as well, which I found nice since it's very flexible.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Condensced introduction to Neuroscience (15 ECTS) 
Immunology (7,5 ECTS)
Introduction to Norway (7,5 ECTS points)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Introduction to Norway was quite a nice course because it was all exchange students and you get an insight into Norwegian culture, society and history. 
Otherwise I loved Immunology since it was very nice lecturers and the topic is really interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I needed more Outdoor equipment than I thought since I wanted to do many activities. A good tip is that you can rent equipment through NTNUI boomerang or BUA for free, just make sure to do it in time as it is very popular. Or ask fellow students/friends if they have equipment to borrow.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Since the norwegian crone was low this year, everything was less expensive than expected. Especially groceries and going out to eat was less expensive.
Outdoor equipment is less expensive than in Denmark, the monthly bus card was less expensive than thought (you could survive without depending on where you live/where you want to go during the week)
Alcohol was pretty expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of sports at NTNUI, student choirs, outdoor groups, winterbathing+sauna groups.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Trondheim really is a student city, they have so many student organisations, choirs, outdoor group etc. I recommend partaking in these, as it is such a nice student milieu. 
In the year I was there, they had UKA which is a Festival in October which is organized by students. I would recommend to join the volunteer work as you meet so many nice people and get to take part in the volunteer work which is really big in Trondheim.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go on hiking trips, either alone or with student organisations such as "NTNUI ski og fjell sport". Use the NTNU koiene (cabins) for overnight stays. 
In winter you should go skiing, both cross country and alpine and use the frozen lakes for ice skating. 
And if you have time/money, it's really worth it to see some of the other citites in Norway as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, since the culture is very similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be a part of all the student organisations, it's very popular to join these and you'll meet a lot of other students. Studentersamfundet is definetely a place where you can get a lot of friends and fun memories, but the other organisations such as NTNUI or ESN are also worth being a part of.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Since Norwegian isn't that far from danish, you can learn to understand it pretty fast. But norwegians tend to talk Norwegian to each other and forget to speak english if there's exchange students, therefore it is important to remember to be including when there's english spearkes, and not speak norwegian/danish even though you understand what the norwegians are saying.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That everyone is nice and welcoming, and if you need any help don't hesitate to ask for it. I also really like that outdoor life and being active is a part of the culture. Furthermore, a lot of students do volunteer work which I liked a lot, without it there would not be half as many student organisations.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take part in the sports and student organisations. Take advantage of the beautiful nature and nice places you can visit in Norway. Remember to enjoy it while you're there, time flies so fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Remember to bring warm clothing and don't underestimate the weather in winter when going on a hike.
Buy equipment in Norway if you don't have any, they have really good equipment stores.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To get to know a lot of people, enjoying the nature and trying to live somewhere else than Denmark.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having to say goodbye to everyone in the end.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I had a lot of friends and family visiting from home, which was nice, but if I could have changed it I might have wanted some more weekends free to go on hiking trips (or asked my friends to join me instead of showing the city).

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
